Name: Apache Kafka
Use Case: Event streaming, CDC backbone, log aggregation, async microservice integration, stream processing source
Strengths: Massive throughput, durable, ordered per-partition, mature ecosystem (Connect, Streams, ksqlDB)
Weaknesses: Operational complexity (ZK history, KRaft now), client tuning surface, no per-message TTL
Cloud Managed Options: MSK (AWS), Confluent Cloud, Aiven, Redpanda Cloud
Keywords: kafka streams kraft connect debezium event log
Notes: Use compacted topics for current-state events; partition by entity id for ordering.

Name: Redpanda
Latency: Lower than Kafka (single binary, no JVM)
Use Case: Drop-in Kafka replacement with simpler ops
Strengths: Single C++ binary, no ZK/JVM, lower p99 latency, full Kafka API
Keywords: redpanda kafka api seastar single binary
Notes: Compelling when ops simplicity matters more than absolute Kafka feature parity.

Name: Apache Pulsar
Use Case: Multi-tenant streaming, geo-replication, mixed queue+stream workloads
Strengths: Multi-tenancy, native geo-replication, separates compute (broker) from storage (BookKeeper)
Keywords: pulsar bookkeeper geo-replication tiered storage multi-tenant
Notes: Functions provide lightweight stream processing inside the cluster.

Name: RabbitMQ
Use Case: Task queues, RPC patterns, complex routing (topic/headers exchanges), classical work queues
Strengths: Mature routing semantics, dead-letter exchanges, plugins, Streams (3.9+)
Weaknesses: Not a log; throughput lower than Kafka; mirrored/quorum queues need careful tuning
Keywords: rabbitmq amqp exchange queue dead letter quorum
Notes: Quorum queues replaced classic mirrored queues for durability; Streams plugin for log-style use.

Name: NATS / NATS JetStream
Use Case: IoT, microservice glue, edge messaging, request/reply at scale
Strengths: Tiny binary, supersonic latency, simple ops, leaf nodes for edge, K/V & Object store
Weaknesses: Smaller ecosystem than Kafka, less BI tooling
Keywords: nats jetstream leaf node request reply edge
Notes: Use JetStream for durability; core NATS for ephemeral pub/sub & RPC.

Name: MQTT (Mosquitto, EMQX, HiveMQ)
Use Case: IoT device telemetry, mobile push backends, low-bandwidth networks
Strengths: Tiny wire format, designed for constrained devices, QoS levels
Weaknesses: Not designed for backend-to-backend high-throughput streaming
Keywords: mqtt iot qos hivemq emqx mosquitto
Notes: Bridge MQTT → Kafka/NATS for downstream stream processing.

Name: AWS SQS
Use Case: Decoupling AWS workloads, retry/DLQ patterns, batch worker fan-out
Strengths: Zero-ops, IAM-integrated, dead-letter queues, FIFO mode
Weaknesses: FIFO has lower TPS, no native broadcast
Keywords: sqs aws queue fifo dlq lambda
Notes: Pair with Lambda + DLQ + maximum receives for resilient async processing.

Name: AWS SNS / EventBridge
Use Case: Fan-out events to many AWS targets, SaaS partner integrations, scheduled events
Strengths: Serverless, native target catalogue, schema registry (EventBridge)
Weaknesses: Vendor-lock to AWS, message size limits
Keywords: sns eventbridge fanout event bus schema registry
Notes: EventBridge Pipes give Kafka-like source→filter→enrich→target with no code.

Name: AWS Kinesis Data Streams
Weaknesses: Lower throughput per shard than Kafka, AWS lock-in
Notes: Use 'on-demand' to avoid manual shard math; 'enhanced fan-out' for multi-consumer.

Name: Google Pub/Sub
Keywords: pubsub gcp google ordering keys exactly-once
Notes: Pub/Sub Lite gives a cheaper, partitioned, log-style alternative.

Name: Azure Service Bus / Event Grid / Event Hubs
Strengths: Three products covering queue / event bus / log
Weaknesses: Three different products to choose between
Cloud Managed Options: Service Bus / Event Grid / Event Hubs
Keywords: service bus event grid event hubs azure
Notes: Event Hubs is Kafka-protocol compatible (good migration path).

Name: ZeroMQ
Use Case: Embedded message patterns inside HPC / robotics / trading apps
Strengths: No broker, blazing fast, rich socket types (REQ/REP, PUB/SUB, PUSH/PULL)
Weaknesses: No persistence, no broker = no central observability
Notes: Great for in-process / cluster-internal patterns; not a backend message bus replacement.
